main_text.p: quid arrogem, fateor, in eo libro nil a-liud esse boni, præter veritatem, cuius semper studiosissimus fui, & diligentiam, qua rerum scripturarum notitiam assequi, exactissime curavi. Quod desideras de Geographia Persici Imperii, non quidem Mathematici, sed potius Historici, ac Politici more, si ea nomina mihi fas usurpare, jam in promptu est: sed Romæ difficilis admodum librorum promulgatio experitur, ob nimium scrupulosas superiorum censuras: longe autem à me parum feliciter hæc typis traderentur, tum ob innumeros voces barbaras, in quarum orthographia si error irreperet, omnia profecto corrumperet, tum etiam quia nomina barbarra locorum, non parva cum utilitate eruditorum legentium, Romæ Persicis etiam characteribns in margine facile possent exarari, quod alibi impossibile futurum existimo, chalcographiæ defectu; verumtamen nihilominus fortasse aliquando illud etiam tibi mittam, ut de eo quod libuerit facias; obscura quæ ad hanc æta-

page.notes: The first word "quid" is printed "qvid" and the sentence begins mid-paragraph, so the paragraph is marked as continuing. The page number "206" is partly obscured by a stain at its head and is marked as doubtful. The final word is split across the foot: "æta-" ends the text and "tem" is the catchword, so the hyphenated word is ætatem. Printing errors left as printed: "barbarra" (for barbara), "characteribns" (for characteribus). Long s was rendered as plain s throughout; "exactissime" and "scripturarum" are read through the scan's long-s forms. Heavy grey show-through and stains fill the left margin; no marginal notes are printed.
